rules: Stop spending proposals on OHLC/return-only expressions: the four price-only accepts scored 0.080, 0.297 and 0.716, while every proposal carrying a fundamental cross-sectional leg or the range-vs-volume corr scored 1.982 to 4.080.

Retire the CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) leading leg. It produced 5 of this round's rejects (5, 7 and 14 shared nodes, one over the edit budget, and rho 0.883 when only the price leg was replaced). A plain CS_RANK($roe)/CS_ZSCORE($roa) leg still pays, but only next to a new kernel.

Changing the wrapper or the field on a fundamental leg does not create distance: CS_RANK to CS_ZSCORE and $roe to $accrual_gap/$asset_turnover left the second leg whole and shared 7 and 14 nodes. Rebuild the price/volume leg instead.

CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($roa, 63)) and CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($asset_turnover, 63)) are spent: three rejects shared exactly those 4 nodes with the archived MIN(...) member regardless of the surrounding operator or the other leg.

Do not select 2-node archive members such as RANK($roa) as crossover parents. Three attempts all shared only 2 nodes because that is the whole parent; pick parents whose donatable subtree is at least 3 nodes.

In the range-vs-volume corr, keep the volume leg a rank/level transform and the window near 42: TS_RANK($volume, 10) against $high - $low at 42 was the top accept (4.080), while TS_STD($dollar_volume, 21) at 63 screened at |t| 0.81 and $return against $high - $low at 21 only reached 0.716.

Mutations that rewrote both sides of a ratio or both legs of a rank spread went 0 for 4 on locality (4 to 6 edits). Change one leg and leave the other's nodes byte-identical; a window plus one leaf is the affordable move.

Two price kernels are dead ends: the overnight gap $open - DELAY($high, 1) under a rank collides with the Alpha#101 family, and $return autocorrelation TS_CORR($return, DELAY($return, 1), 21) screened at |t| 0.35.
